summary: MPEG-V Part 3 (ISO/IEC 23005-3) defines how to describe effects for senses other than sight and hearing, such as light, wind, fog, vibration, temperature, scent and touch, so they can accompany audio-visual content. It supplies a description language and a vocabulary of named effects; the fourth edition of 2019 added an arrayed light effect. It does not say how an effect becomes commands for a particular device: that adaptation step is expressly left out, and the description of device capabilities and user preferences, avatars, sensor data formats, profiles and conformance tests sit in other parts of the series. Only the public preview of the 2019 edition could be read (contents, foreword, introduction and scope), not the paid full text and not the 2016 edition named in the subject record, so effect rules are scored from clause headings only. One trap: a recent research paper reports that how effects are signalled and carried alongside audio-visual streams through a distribution chain is still unresolved, even though the standard exists.

coverage.note: Part 3 describes touch-related effects: vibration, tactile, parameterized tactile, passive and active kinesthetic motion and force. Only the clause headings and introduction of the public preview were read; the detailed rules are in the paid text.
